parameters.content:
## Personalized welcome video for every trial signup

A new user signs up → your product POSTs their name, plan and company to the
webhook → Zvid renders a 15-second branded welcome video (1920×1080, made for
the welcome email) → the webhook response returns the video URL plus an editor
link. Optionally it emails the video for you.

### Setup (about three minutes)

1. **Zvid API key** — create one at https://app.zvid.io/api-keys
   Add an n8n **Header Auth** credential: name `x-api-key`, value = your key.
   Attach it to *Validate project (free)*, *Save draft to editor*,
   *Submit render* and *Get render status*.
2. **Open `Config`** and set your brand: `brandName`, colours, `ctaText`,
   `ctaUrl` and the three onboarding cards.
3. Click **Execute workflow** — the *Test manually* trigger feeds the
   *Sample signup*. **`dryRun` is `false`, so this renders for real and
   spends credits (about 15).** You get a finished MP4: click the
   **▶ Watch video** node at the end to play it right here.
   Prefer a free preview? Set `dryRun: true` in **Config** first — it
   validates, quotes the credits and returns an **editorLink** to the
   draft, charging nothing.
4. Point your signup flow at the production webhook URL. Nothing else to
   flip: with `dryRun: false`, every signup gets a rendered video.

### Cost

A 15-second welcome video is **about 15 Zvid credits** at the defaults. The
free validate step returns that exact quote before every render, and the
render then proceeds automatically — set `dryRun: true` to see the quote
without spending. Free accounts include enough credits to test.

## The webhook contract

POST JSON to this workflow's webhook URL:

```
{
  "firstName": "Maya",        ← required
  "plan": "Pro trial",
  "company": "Northwind Labs",
  "email": "maya@example.com" ← optional, used by the email step
}
```

The response is sent when the run finishes:
`{ videoUrl, editorLink, dryRun, creditsCharged, jobId, ... }`
(on an opt-in dry run, `videoUrl` is `null` and the quote arrives as
`creditsRequired` instead)

**A real render is the default, and it keeps the HTTP request open for one
to three minutes** while the video renders — raise your caller's timeout, or
turn on `sendEmail` and treat the webhook as fire-and-forget. Opt-in dry runs
(`dryRun: true`) answer in a few seconds.

## Make it yours

Everything lives in **Config** — the design adapts automatically:

- `brandName`, `brandAccent`, `brandBackground`, `brandGlow` — colours flow
  into every scene, chip, card and button.
- `brandLogoUrl` — URL of a square logo image. Leave it empty to get a clean
  monogram tile generated from `brandName`.
- `cards` — the three "what to do first" steps. Keep titles under ~30
  characters and details under ~110 so nothing crowds the card.
- Copy knobs may embed `{firstName}`, `{plan}`, `{company}` and `{brand}` —
  replaced with the signup's real values and HTML-escaped.
- Long values are safe: the headline auto-shrinks in steps (tested down to a
  hyphenated 21-character first name and a 46-character company name), and
  the plan chip renders whatever `plan` your product sends, uppercased.

## Free preview — opt in with `dryRun: true`

This workflow renders for real by default (`dryRun: false` in **Config**).
Set `dryRun: true` and it stops before the paid render: it validates the
project, saves it as a **draft** and answers the webhook with an
**editorLink** like `https://editor.zvid.io/?project=prj_...` — no credits
spent, and `creditsRequired` carries the exact quote.

Open the link to watch the draft and tweak it by hand. Set `dryRun` back to
`false` to render the finished MP4.

## Optional: email the video

`sendEmail` in **Config** is **false** by default. Turn it on and the
workflow emails the finished video link to the `email` field from the
webhook payload (the step is skipped when the payload has no email).

The node is n8n's core **Send Email** (SMTP) — attach any SMTP credential.
**On n8n Cloud, swap this node for the Gmail node** (or Outlook) in one
click; everything upstream stays identical.

Tip: many teams instead paste `videoUrl` into their existing email
platform — the webhook response returns it either way.

## Official Zvid nodes

These HTTP Request nodes are deliberately core-only so the workflow runs
anywhere, including n8n Cloud with nothing installed.

On self-hosted n8n you can install **`@zvid/n8n-nodes-zvid`**
(Settings → Community nodes) and swap:

| HTTP Request node | Native replacement |
| --- | --- |
| Validate project (free) | **Zvid** → Render → Validate |
| Submit render | **Zvid** → Render → Create |
| Get render status + Wait | **Zvid Trigger** (render webhook) |

The Zvid Trigger removes the polling loop entirely.

## ▶ Watch it right here

Click **▶ Watch video** and n8n plays the finished MP4 in the output panel —
the node downloads it as binary `video/mp4`, which n8n renders as an inline
player with a download button. No copying URLs out of a JSON blob.

It hangs off *Render response*, which still carries `videoUrl`, `editorLink`
and `jobId` for piping onward — and *Respond to signup* still answers the
caller first, untouched. Only real renders reach this node; a dry run never
does.
